subject.title: ci: harden HTTP and local-auth gates against transient failures

question: Should maintainers split the HTTP fixture failure from the local-auth saturation work, and which mitigation should be funded and landed first?
rationale: The two causes have different owners and validation paths, while runner sizing changes CI cost and could mask application or test load amplification without capacity measurements.

options.title: Split and diagnose first
options.body: Create separate HTTP and local-auth implementation tracks, add runner/quota and timeout diagnostics first, then land targeted mitigations with bounded soak validation.

options.title: Keep one reliability issue
options.body: Retain this umbrella issue and sequence all HTTP, runner, retry, and profile-query changes under one coordinated maintainer-owned effort.

options.title: Capacity-only mitigation
options.body: Increase or relocate heavy shard capacity first and defer query and retry changes until new failure data is collected.

recommendation.title: Split and diagnose first
recommendation.body: Create separate HTTP and local-auth implementation tracks, add runner/quota and timeout diagnostics first, then land targeted mitigations with bounded soak validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged ownership signal is the recent cross-gate and local-auth CI stabilization work.
